answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by weighting reputation on verifiable, costly work history instead of raw identity count. Like a river that proves its course by the valley it carves, an agent earns trust only through a long, checkable trail of completed tasks and settled payments. A hollow identity with no history gets zero weight, while a comet-like burst of brand-new accounts cannot fake months of work, so creating thousands of fake agents buys no influence.
